experiences.name: Diavolezza Glacier Skiing
experiences.description: Experience world-class skiing on the Diavolezza glacier near Pontresina, offering stunning runs with panoramic views of Piz Palü and Bernina peaks. Suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers with over 10km of marked pistes and off-piste opportunities.

experiences.name: Bernina Express Scenic Winter Rail Journey
experiences.description: Board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express from Poschiavo station, winding through dramatic Alpine landscapes, frozen lakes, and snow-covered viaducts. The route passes the famous Brusio spiral viaduct just minutes from Poschiavo, offering breathtaking winter scenery.
experiences.location: Poschiavo Railway Station, Via Principale, Poschiavo

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails
experiences.description: Explore serene cross-country ski trails departing from Alp Grüm, a high-altitude stop above Poschiavo accessible by the Bernina railway. Glide through pristine snow with sweeping views of the Palü glacier and the Poschiavo valley below.

experiences.name: Snowshoeing in Val da Camp
experiences.description: Strap on snowshoes and trek through the enchanting Val da Camp side valley near Poschiavo, a quiet and pristine winter wilderness. Guided tours reveal local Alpine flora, frozen waterfalls, and traditional Graubünden stone farmhouses buried in snow.

experiences.name: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with an authentic Graubünden dinner in Poschiavo's historic village center. Savor local cheese fondue, hearty Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with alpine cheese and vegetables), and Valtellina wines in a cozy centuries-old stone restaurant.
experiences.location: Historic Village Center, Via Principale, Poschiavo

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30. Rest and prepare for the week ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30. Take the train toward Chur and then connect toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express or regional rail. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama upon arrival (late check-in — confirm with host in advance). Unpack and settle in.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: On the plane or grab a quick bite at Zurich Airport (budget tip: Migros or Coop supermarket inside the airport for sandwiches under CHF 8).
meals.dinner: Pick up snacks and essentials at a convenience store or vending machine at the train station en route — arrival is late so dining options will be limited.

day_by_day.notes: The train journey from Zurich to Poschiavo takes approximately 3.5–4 hours with connections. Book tickets in advance via SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) for the best budget fares. Confirm late check-in arrangements with the B&B host before arrival. Keep CHF cash on hand as smaller villages may not accept cards everywhere.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a hearty B&B breakfast included with your stay. Take a leisurely morning walk through the charming village of Poschiavo — explore the historic Piazza Comunale, the Spanish-style houses, and the Reformed Church. Get oriented with the local area and pick up a trail map from the tourist office.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Poschiavo Valley slopes for a beginner-friendly introduction to the local ski scene. Rent budget ski equipment from a local rental shop in Poschiavo (approx. CHF 25–35/day for skis, boots, and poles). Explore the gentle slopes near the valley floor or take the Bernina Express train up toward Alp Grüm to scout the cross-country ski trails for the next day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village. Stroll along the main street as the Alpine sunset paints the mountains golden. Warm up with a hot chocolate or Glühwein at a local café.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget lunch at the Coop or local bakery in Poschiavo — pick up a panino or local pastry for under CHF 10.
meals.dinner: Dine at Ristorante Croce Federale in Poschiavo — a local favorite offering hearty Graubünden specialties like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and polenta for CHF 15–22 per main course.

day_by_day.notes: Poschiavo sits at about 1,014m elevation. The Bernina Express train (Poschiavo to Alp Grüm) is a UNESCO World Heritage route and a budget-friendly way to access higher elevations — a single ticket costs approximately CHF 10–15. Validate your Swiss Travel Pass if you have one, as it may cover regional trains.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early and take the Bernina Express train from Poschiavo up to Alp Grüm station (elevation ~2,091m). Begin the Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails experience — glide through serene, groomed cross-country ski trails with breathtaking panoramic views of the Palü Glacier and surrounding peaks. The trails are well-marked and suitable for intermediate skiers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Alp Grüm cross-country network. Take a break at the Rifugio Alp Grüm (mountain hut) for a warm drink and to soak in the stunning Alpine scenery. Attempt the longer loop trails if energy permits, passing through snow-covered forests and open Alpine meadows.
day_by_day.evening: Take the train back down to Poschiavo. Warm up at the B&B and freshen up. Enjoy a relaxed evening in the village.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast before departing — fuel up well for a full day of skiing.
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade lunch from the B&B or buy supplies the night before — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and a thermos of hot tea or coffee. Eating at the mountain hut is an option but costs more (CHF 15–25 for a meal).
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using the B&B kitchen if available, or visit Osteria Salis in Poschiavo for affordable local cuisine — try the Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup) and local sausages for around CHF 18–25.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski rental is available in Poschiavo or sometimes at Alp Grüm — call ahead to confirm availability (approx. CHF 20–30/day). Dress in moisture-wicking layers as cross-country skiing is aerobically intense. Bring sunscreen — UV rays are intense at altitude even in winter. The train to Alp Grüm runs regularly; check the SBB timetable the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express north toward St. Moritz (approximately 45 minutes from Poschiavo). Explore the famous resort town on a budget — walk around the frozen Lake St. Moritz, admire the luxury hotels from the outside, and visit the free Segantini Museum exterior and the village center. The lake often hosts free spectator events in winter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz. Purchase a half-day ski pass (afternoon, approx. CHF 45–55) for access to well-groomed intermediate and advanced runs with spectacular Engadin Valley views. Rent equipment if needed from the base area rental shops. Ski until the lifts close around 16:30.
day_by_day.evening: Return by train to Poschiavo. Enjoy a quiet evening at the B&B — review photos, plan the next day, and rest tired muscles.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast — eat well before the day trip.
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch to eat on the mountain or at the base area — this saves CHF 20–30 compared to on-mountain restaurants. Alternatively, grab a bratwurst from a mountain kiosk (CHF 6–8).
meals.dinner: Stop at the Coop supermarket in St. Moritz before heading back to pick up ready-made meals or ingredients (CHF 8–15). Alternatively, cook at the B&B or dine at a local Poschiavo trattoria.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of Switzerland's most expensive resorts, but visiting as a day tripper and bringing your own food keeps costs manageable. The train from Poschiavo to St. Moritz costs approximately CHF 15–20 each way (check Swiss Travel Pass coverage). A full-day ski pass at Corviglia costs CHF 70–80 — opt for a half-day pass to save money. Lockers at the base area cost CHF 3–5.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Poschiavo Valley on snowshoes — rent snowshoes locally (approx. CHF 15–20/day) and follow the marked snowshoe trail from Poschiavo toward Le Prese along the valley floor beside the frozen Lake Poschiavo. The trail is flat, scenic, and free to use. Enjoy the peaceful winter landscape and views of the surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the snowshoe loop around Lake Poschiavo (Lago di Poschiavo) — the full circuit is approximately 8–10 km and takes 2.5–3 hours at a leisurely pace. Stop at the small village of Le Prese for a warm drink at a local café before heading back. Alternatively, rent ice skates at the natural ice rink if conditions allow (free or minimal fee).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. Visit the local Museo di Poschiavo (small admission fee ~CHF 5) to learn about the valley's unique cultural history — Poschiavo has a fascinating mix of Swiss-Italian heritage. Enjoy a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the snowshoe trail — prepare sandwiches and hot drinks in a thermos from the B&B. Budget: CHF 5–8 in supplies.
meals.dinner: Try Pizzeria da Rino in Poschiavo for affordable wood-fired pizza and pasta — a filling meal for CHF 14–20. A great budget-friendly option with generous portions.

day_by_day.notes: Lake Poschiavo is a beautiful and underrated winter destination. The snowshoe trail is well-marked but check local conditions with the tourist office. This is a great low-cost day — snowshoe rental and the trail itself are very affordable. Bring trekking poles if available for added stability on icy sections.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express south toward Tirano, Italy (just across the Swiss-Italian border — approximately 20 minutes from Poschiavo). Explore the charming Italian town of Tirano, visit the stunning Basilica di Madonna di Tirano (free entry), and browse the local market. Stock up on affordable Italian groceries, wine, and snacks — prices are significantly lower than in Switzerland.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Poschiavo by early afternoon. Head back up toward Alp Grüm for a second session of cross-country skiing or snowshoeing, this time exploring different trail variations you may have missed on Day 3. The afternoon light on the glacier is particularly beautiful for photography.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your penultimate evening in the Alps with a special budget dinner. Cook a meal using Italian ingredients purchased in Tirano — pasta, local cheese, and wine make for a wonderful and affordable feast at the B&B.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast — early start for the Tirano day trip.
meals.lunch: Eat in Tirano, Italy — a full meal at a local trattoria costs EUR 10–15 (significantly cheaper than Switzerland). Try local Valtellina specialties like pizzoccheri or bresaola.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at the B&B using Italian groceries from Tirano — pasta, local cheese, salumi, and a bottle of Valtellina wine for under CHF 20 total.

day_by_day.notes: You will need your passport to cross into Italy, even as a day tripper (Switzerland is not in the EU but border crossings are generally smooth). The Bernina Express to Tirano is covered by the Swiss Travel Pass to the Swiss border — you pay a small supplement for the Italian section (approx. EUR 3–5). Tirano is a great budget hack for stocking up on affordable food and wine for the rest of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — wake up early for one last sunrise walk or snowshoe around Poschiavo village. Visit the weekly Sunday market if running (check locally). Pack your bags and check out of the B&B. Store luggage with the host if possible for a few extra hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend your final afternoon on a farewell ski or snowshoe session on the Alp Grüm trails — a shorter 2-hour outing to soak in the mountain air one last time. Alternatively, take a scenic train ride on the Bernina Express toward Ospizio Bernina (the highest point on the line at 2,253m) for dramatic views of the Bernina massif — no skiing required, just a spectacular train journey.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the journey home — take the train from Poschiavo toward Chur and then to Zurich for onward connections. Enjoy the scenic Bernina and Rhine Valley views as you descend from the Alps.

meals.breakfast: Final B&B breakfast — savor it!
meals.lunch: Grab a farewell meal at a local Poschiavo café or use up remaining groceries for a picnic. Budget CHF 10–15.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Zurich Airport or on the train — pick up a meal deal at the Coop or Migros at the station (CHF 10–15) for an affordable final meal before your flight.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and allow ample travel time — Poschiavo to Zurich Airport takes approximately 3.5–4 hours by train. Book return train tickets in advance via SBB for the best prices. Leave a review for the B&B and tip your host if the service was excellent — a small gesture goes a long way in family-run establishments.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport on flight UA at 22:30. Transfer by train or pre-arranged shuttle toward Poschiavo. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle into your room and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in transit)
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or sandwich at the airport or train station during transfer — budget CHF 10–15

day_by_day.notes: The journey from Zurich to Poschiavo takes approximately 3.5–4 hours by train (via Chur and the Rhaetian Railway). From Milan Malpensa it is roughly 3 hours by train via Tirano. Confirm transfer logistics with your B&B in advance. Pack layers — Poschiavo sits at 1,014 m and February nights are cold.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely B&B breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk through Poschiavo's charming historic village centre — admire the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish-style houses, and the frozen Lago di Poschiavo. This easy stroll helps you acclimatise to the altitude and get your bearings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snowshoeing in Val da Camp — strap on snowshoes (rentable in Poschiavo for ~CHF 15–20/day) and explore the quiet, enchanting Val da Camp side valley. The trail winds through snow-draped forests and open meadows with stunning mountain backdrops. Suitable for beginners; the round trip is approximately 3–4 hours at a relaxed pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo village and warm up with a Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner at a local restaurant in the historic centre. Pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables) is the regional speciality — a perfect hearty end to your first full day.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast included at your accommodation
meals.lunch: Pack a simple picnic from a local bakery or deli in Poschiavo before heading to Val da Camp — budget CHF 10–15 (bread, cheese, cured meats, hot thermos of tea)
meals.dinner: Traditional Graubünden dinner at a local Poschiavo restaurant — expect CHF 30–45 per person for fondue or pizzoccheri with a glass of local Valtellina wine

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe rentals are available at sports shops in Poschiavo. Val da Camp is accessed by a short drive or taxi from the village. Check trail conditions with your B&B host. Stay hydrated — altitude can cause mild fatigue on your first full day.

day_by_day.morning: Diavolezza Glacier Skiing — take the Rhaetian Railway or drive (~45 min) to Pontresina/Diavolezza. Board the Diavolezza cable car and enjoy world-class skiing on the glacier. Morning sessions offer the best snow conditions and fewer crowds. The glacier runs are spectacular, with panoramic views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Day ski pass approximately CHF 65–75.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza, exploring different runs across the glacier and the Lagalb ski area (linked). Try the famous Diavolezza descent — a 10 km off-piste glacier run (with a guide if needed). Take a mid-afternoon break at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant for a hot drink and a slice of apple strudel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train or car. Freshen up at the B&B, then enjoy a relaxed dinner in the village. Try Ristorante Suisse or a similar mid-range local spot for hearty Alpine cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast included
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant at Diavolezza — budget CHF 20–30 for a hot meal (rösti, soup, or pasta)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Poschiavo village — CHF 25–40 per person for a main course and drink

day_by_day.notes: Purchase ski passes online in advance to save time and occasionally money. Ski and boot rentals are available at Pontresina or Diavolezza base (~CHF 45–55/day). The Rhaetian Railway from Poschiavo to Pontresina requires a change at Ospizio Bernina — allow 1 hour travel time each way. Dress in waterproof ski layers.

day_by_day.morning: Bernina Express Scenic Winter Rail Journey — board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express from Poschiavo station. Travel northward through dramatic Alpine scenery: the Brusio spiral viaduct, frozen Lago Bianco, and snow-covered Bernina Pass (2,253 m). Ride to St. Moritz or Pontresina for a morning of exploration. The journey from Poschiavo to St. Moritz takes about 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore St. Moritz — stroll along the frozen lake, browse the village, and optionally watch or participate in winter activities on the lake (ice skating, kite skiing, or simply spectating). Visit the Segantini Museum if you enjoy Alpine art. Return to Poschiavo on the afternoon Bernina Express, soaking in the scenery again from the other direction.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the B&B or in Poschiavo. Enjoy a lighter dinner at a local café or pizzeria — a good mid-week rest evening before more active days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast included — eat early before catching the morning train
meals.lunch: Lunch in St. Moritz — try a mid-range café or bakery; budget CHF 20–35 per person (St. Moritz has options across all price ranges)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner in Poschiavo — local pizzeria or café, CHF 18–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Bernina Express rail pass or point-to-point ticket: approximately CHF 30–50 round trip from Poschiavo to St. Moritz (Swiss Travel Pass holders ride free or at discount). Book seats in advance for panoramic car windows. The Brusio spiral viaduct is best viewed from the right-hand side heading north — sit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Cross-Country Skiing on Alp Grüm Trails — take the Rhaetian Railway one stop up from Poschiavo to Alp Grüm (2,091 m), a dramatic high-altitude station perched above the valley. Rent cross-country skis (~CHF 20–30/day) and explore the serene groomed trails with sweeping views over the Palü glacier and into Italy. The trails suit all levels and offer a peaceful contrast to downhill skiing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cross-country skiing or snowshoeing around Alp Grüm. The area is wonderfully quiet on weekdays. Take time to sit at the Alp Grüm restaurant terrace with a hot chocolate and absorb the extraordinary panorama before heading back down to Poschiavo by train in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner — if you haven't already had the full fondue experience, tonight is the perfect night. Join a communal table at a local Poschiavo restaurant and enjoy cheese fondue with local bread, accompanied by a glass of Graubünden Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast included
meals.lunch: Alp Grüm mountain restaurant — simple, hearty Alpine lunch; budget CHF 18–28 (soup, rösti, or a hot sandwich)
meals.dinner: Traditional fondue dinner in Poschiavo — CHF 30–45 per person including wine

day_by_day.notes: The train from Poschiavo to Alp Grüm takes about 20 minutes and runs regularly. Cross-country ski rentals may need to be arranged in Poschiavo before boarding the train. Alp Grüm can be very cold and windy — bring an extra insulating layer and windproof jacket. Sunscreen is essential at altitude even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Diavolezza for a second day of downhill skiing — now that you know the mountain, explore runs you missed on Day 3. Consider hiring a local ski guide for a half-day to access more challenging terrain or the famous off-piste glacier descent safely (~CHF 80–120 for a shared group guide). Saturday may be busier — arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski until early afternoon, then head back toward Pontresina. Stop in Pontresina village for a browse of the charming main street, visit a local sports shop, or enjoy a coffee at a café before returning to Poschiavo. Alternatively, if snow conditions allow, try the Lagalb ski area (linked to Diavolezza) for a change of scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory penultimate evening dinner — treat yourself to the best meal of the trip at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant in Poschiavo or nearby. Look for a restaurant serving Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), venison, or other regional specialities. Pair with a local Graubünden wine.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast included — eat well before a full ski day
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant at Diavolezza or Lagalb — CHF 20–30 for a hot meal
meals.dinner: Best dinner of the trip — mid-range restaurant in Poschiavo, CHF 40–55 per person with wine; consider booking ahead on a Saturday

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is the busiest day on the slopes — purchase lift tickets online the night before. If the glacier descent is on your list, confirm guide availability and book in advance. Check avalanche bulletins (slf.ch) before any off-piste activity. Return trains from Pontresina to Poschiavo run hourly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely last B&B breakfast. Take a slow walk around Poschiavo village one more time, visit the local Sunday market if running, pick up souvenirs (local cheese, Bündner Nusstorte nut tart, or Graubünden wine) from a village shop or deli. Pack and check out of the B&B.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight or train, take one final scenic ride on the Bernina Express toward Tirano (Italy) or Chur for your onward connection. The southbound journey to Tirano (45 min) passes the spectacular Brusio viaduct and offers a beautiful farewell to the Alps. Alternatively, if time allows, a final short snowshoe walk near the village before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Travel day — transfer to your departure airport (Zurich ~4 hrs, Milan Malpensa ~2.5 hrs from Tirano). Enjoy a final Swiss or Italian meal at the airport or en route.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast included — savour your last Alpine morning meal
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Poschiavo before departure or on the train — local bakery or café, CHF 12–18
meals.dinner: Airport or transit dinner — budget CHF 20–35 depending on location

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with your B&B host and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. The Bernina Express to Tirano connects to trains toward Milan and Malpensa airport. For Zurich departures, head north via Chur. Book return train tickets in advance on weekends. Allow extra time for luggage and winter gear at the airport.

day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late check-in at B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. A welcome amenity tray with local Graubünden wines, artisan cheeses, and warm herbal tea should be pre-arranged with the property. Settle in, unpack, and rest ahead of a full alpine adventure week.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit or airport dining at Zurich/Milan depending on routing
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome spread arranged by the B&B: local charcuterie, Bündner Nusstorte, herbal tea, and a glass of Valtellina Superiore red wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (Mercedes V-Class or similar) from your arrival airport to Poschiavo — approximately 2.5 hours from Zurich or 1.5 hours from Milan Malpensa. Confirm late check-in with the property in advance. Keep Day 2 morning relaxed to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late breakfast at the B&B to recover from travel. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk through Poschiavo's beautifully preserved historic village center — explore the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo), the Baroque church of San Vittore, and the charming main piazza. Pick up any last-minute ski gear or rentals from a local sports shop in Poschiavo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the iconic UNESCO-listed Bernina Express scenic winter rail journey from Poschiavo station. Wind through dramatic alpine landscapes, frozen viaducts, and snow-draped forests toward Pontresina and St. Moritz. Enjoy panoramic views from the comfort of the panoramic carriages. Use this journey as a scenic reconnaissance of the region before full ski days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Freshen up at the B&B and head out for a Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner in Poschiavo's historic village — warm up with authentic regional cuisine including buckwheat pizzoccheri pasta with Valtellina Casera cheese, and a classic cheese fondue paired with local Poschiavo wines.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at B&B Berninahaus Panorama — fresh local bread, Engadine honey, cold cuts, soft-boiled eggs, and freshly brewed coffee with mountain views
meals.lunch: Onboard the Bernina Express — pre-book the dining car service for a curated lunch of regional soups, open-faced sandwiches, and Swiss pastries while the alpine scenery unfolds
meals.dinner: Traditional Graubünden dinner at a top-rated Poschiavo restaurant such as Ristorante Suisse or Albergo Croce Federale — pizzoccheri al forno, cheese fondue, local Sforzato wine, and Bündner Nusstorte for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book Bernina Express panoramic carriage seats well in advance through Rhaetian Railway (RhB) — first-class seats recommended for the luxury experience. The round trip from Poschiavo to St. Moritz and back is approximately 3–4 hours total. Confirm restaurant reservation for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for a full day of world-class skiing at Diavolezza Glacier. Drive or take the Bernina Express to Pontresina/Diavolezza cable car station (approx. 30–40 minutes from Poschiavo). Ascend to 3,000m on the Diavolezza cable car and begin morning runs on the glacier's legendary wide pistes with breathtaking views of Piz Palü, Piz Bernina, and the Morteratsch Glacier. Hire a private ski guide for personalized instruction and access to the best off-piste routes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza — explore the famous Diavolezza-Lagalb ski area with varied terrain suitable for intermediate to advanced skiers. Take the iconic off-piste glacier descent toward Morteratsch (with guide). Enjoy a mid-afternoon break on the sun terrace of the Diavolezza mountain restaurant with panoramic glacier views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by late afternoon. Indulge in a premium après-ski experience — book a private spa session or hot tub soak if available at or near the B&B. Dinner at a refined local restaurant featuring Graubünden specialties.

meals.breakfast: Hearty alpine breakfast at the B&B — muesli, yogurt, local honey, eggs to order, fresh pastries, and strong espresso to fuel a full ski day
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Diavolezza Mountain Restaurant (3,000m altitude) — enjoy rösti with mountain cheese, hearty alpine soup, and a glass of Glühwein on the sun terrace with glacier panoramas
meals.dinner: Elegant dinner at Ristorante Palazzo Salis or equivalent fine dining in Poschiavo — venison ragù, truffle risotto, and a curated selection from the Graubünden wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book a certified private ski guide through Pontresina or St. Moritz ski schools for the glacier descent — essential for safety on off-piste terrain. Rent premium ski equipment (Völkl, Rossignol, or Atomic) from a Pontresina ski shop if not bringing your own. Diavolezza lift pass can be purchased as a day pass or as part of the Engadin St. Moritz ski area pass.

day_by_day.morning: Active morning with cross-country skiing on the Alp Grüm trails. Board the Bernina Express or Rhaetian Railway from Poschiavo up to Alp Grüm station (a stunning high-altitude stop perched above the valley). Strap on cross-country skis and glide through serene, groomed trails with sweeping views over the Palü Glacier and the Italian Alps. This is a peaceful, meditative contrast to the high-speed downhill days.
day_by_day.afternoon: After cross-country skiing, descend back toward Poschiavo and transition to a snowshoeing adventure in Val da Camp — a quiet, enchanting side valley near Poschiavo. Trek through pristine snow-covered forests and meadows, spotting winter wildlife tracks and enjoying the silence of the untouched alpine wilderness. A local guide can enhance the experience with knowledge of the valley's flora, fauna, and history.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the B&B for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private wine tasting of Valtellina and Graubünden wines arranged at the property, or visit a local enoteca. Light but refined dinner to rest the legs.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast with extra protein focus — scrambled eggs, smoked salmon, whole grain bread, fresh fruit, and a double espresso
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on the Alp Grüm trails — pre-arrange a luxury packed lunch from the B&B or a local deli: thermos of hot soup, artisan sandwiches, Swiss chocolate, dried fruits, and a flask of hot herbal tea
meals.dinner: Cozy dinner at a Poschiavo trattoria — handmade pasta, braised local beef, polenta taragna, and a bottle of Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG

day_by_day.notes: Alp Grüm is accessible only by the Rhaetian Railway — no road access — making it a uniquely peaceful alpine destination. Snowshoe rentals are available in Poschiavo. Book a local nature guide for the Val da Camp snowshoe trek through the Poschiavo tourist office or local guiding agencies. Dress in moisture-wicking layers as cross-country skiing generates significant body heat.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Diavolezza for a second premium ski day, this time focusing on the Lagalb ski area on the opposite side of the Bernina Pass — a more challenging, less-crowded mountain with steep runs and excellent powder fields. Take the first cable car up for fresh tracks on groomed pistes. Explore the varied terrain with your private guide, including some of the steeper couloirs if conditions permit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Mid-afternoon, transition to a heli-skiing or snowcat skiing experience if available through local operators in the Engadin valley — the ultimate luxury alpine experience offering access to untouched powder fields far from the crowds. Alternatively, enjoy a leisurely afternoon of free skiing at Diavolezza with time to perfect technique on the glacier runs.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the penultimate ski day with a special dinner — book a table at one of the finest restaurants in the Poschiavo or Pontresina area. Consider a private chef dinner experience at the B&B if arrangeable, featuring a curated tasting menu of regional Alpine cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Power breakfast at the B&B — protein-rich spread with eggs Benedict style, smoked meats, fresh orange juice, and barista-quality coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Berghaus Lagalb or the Diavolezza mountain restaurant — grilled sausages, alpine macaroni (Älplermagronen), and a warming Bombardino cocktail (egg liqueur with whipped cream)
meals.dinner: Premium tasting menu dinner — book at Ristorante Suisse Poschiavo or arrange a private chef experience at the B&B featuring 5-course Alpine tasting menu: amuse-bouche, venison carpaccio, truffle soup, braised chamois, cheese course, and Engadine nut tart with vanilla gelato

day_by_day.notes: Heli-skiing in Switzerland requires advance booking and is subject to weather and regulatory conditions — contact Air Engiadina or local operators well in advance. Ensure comprehensive travel and ski insurance covers off-piste and heli-skiing activities. The Lagalb ski area day pass is separate from Diavolezza — consider purchasing the combined Engadin St. Moritz area pass for flexibility.

day_by_day.morning: A more relaxed morning — sleep in slightly and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the B&B. Mid-morning, take a scenic snowshoe walk directly from the property through the Poschiavo valley floor, exploring the frozen Lake Poschiavo (Lago di Poschiavo) shoreline. The lake in winter is a magical, glassy expanse surrounded by snow-dusted peaks — ideal for photography and quiet reflection.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the Bernina Express for a premium full scenic round trip — this time heading north through the Bernina Pass to Ospizio Bernina (the highest point of the line at 2,253m) and continuing to Pontresina or St. Moritz for an afternoon of luxury shopping and exploration. Browse the boutiques of St. Moritz's Via Serlas — Cartier, Bulgari, Moncler, and local Swiss watchmakers. Enjoy the glamorous resort atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by early evening. Final Traditional Graubünden Fondue & Pizzoccheri Dinner experience — this time at a different venue or with a private dining arrangement to mark the last full evening. Toast the week with a bottle of aged Sforzato or a premium Swiss Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast at the B&B — full spread with champagne or Prosecco to mark the final full day, fresh croissants, local jams, artisan cheeses, and a full hot option
meals.lunch: Lunch in St. Moritz at Roo Bar, Kulm Hotel, or Badrutt's Palace Hotel restaurant — enjoy a refined alpine lunch in one of the world's most iconic ski resort settings
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo — private dining arrangement at the B&B or a reserved table at the best local restaurant: multi-course meal featuring pizzoccheri, cheese fondue, local game, and a dessert of Torta di Pane (Graubünden bread cake) with aged grappa

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is approximately 45–50 minutes from Poschiavo by Bernina Express — a first-class return ticket is recommended. The frozen Lake Poschiavo walk is approximately 2–3 km and suitable without specialized equipment in good conditions — check ice safety with locals before venturing onto the lake surface. Pre-arrange the farewell dinner reservation well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Swiss Alps — wake up early for one last sunrise view from the B&B terrace over the Poschiavo valley. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast. If time permits before checkout, take a short 30-minute walk through Poschiavo village to pick up last-minute souvenirs: Bündner Nusstorte, local honey, Graubünden wines, and Swiss chocolates from the village shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of B&B Berninahaus Poschiavo Panorama. Private luxury transfer departs for your onward destination — Zurich Airport (approx. 2.5 hours), Milan Malpensa (approx. 1.5 hours), or another Swiss city. If the flight is late afternoon or evening, consider a brief stop in Lugano or Bellinzona en route for a final Swiss lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary week of world-class skiing, breathtaking alpine scenery, and authentic Graubünden culture in one of Switzerland's most beautiful and underrated valleys.

meals.breakfast: Final farewell breakfast at the B&B — the full spread one last time, savoring every moment of the alpine morning with fresh coffee and mountain views
meals.lunch: Depending on transfer routing: lunch at a lakeside restaurant in Lugano (Ristorante Galleria Arté al Lago) or a quick but quality stop at a Swiss motorway service area with local specialties, or airport lounge dining
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dinner or onboard premium cabin dining — or a final Swiss restaurant meal if departure is late evening

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange the private luxury transfer for checkout day well in advance — Sunday transfers can be limited in this region. Allow extra time for mountain road conditions in February. Confirm luggage storage at the B&B if checkout is before the transfer departs. Tip the B&B staff generously for any exceptional service during the stay. Ensure all ski equipment rentals are returned before departure.

query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February
